subject: Clarify: Pricing Exhibit — variable anchor band & earnback mechanics
messages:
From: Contracts (NovaPlex) <contracts@novaplex.io>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendez <sofia@novaplex.io>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: NovaPlex - Order Form redline: pricing exhibit questions

Connor — attaching our redline of the Order Form (pricing exhibit). We have three substantive asks we need clarity on before routing to our procurement/legal approvers:

1) "Anchor band" / variable band: your draft ties the effective per-token rates to a quarterlyized anchor band that adjusts up or down based on trailing three-month usage. Our procurement team is concerned this could create retroactive refunds for overcrediting at low usage months. Can you confirm whether the band adjustment is prospective (applies from next quarter) or truly retroactive?

2) Earnback / smoothing: the proposed earnback mechanism in section 2(b) allows for an earnback credit when monthly usage drops below the floor. We need the formula clarified (is it prorated on committed months or on billed tokens?) and a maximum cap on cumulative earnback.

3) Early-exit trueup: your redline states a 12-month trueup window. Our CFO prefers a 6-month settlement to protect cashflows. Is Redwood open to a shorter trueup period or an interim settlement if variance exceeds 40%?

Attached: NovaPlex_OrderForm_REDLINED.pdf (redline), summary comments in DOCX.

Thanks — please route to finance/legal as needed. We need final language this week.

—Marta Lopez
Senior Contracts Specialist
NovaPlex, Inc.
attachments: NovaPlex_OrderForm_REDLINED.pdf (pdf), npx-commentary.docx (docx)

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Contracts (NovaPlex) <contracts@novaplex.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovaPlex - Order Form redline: pricing exhibit questions

Marta — really appreciate the clear redline and the timing expectation. Quick responses below; looping in Lauren and Karthik for legal/finance validation and to propose specific draft language.

- Anchor band adjustments: our intention is for the anchor band to be forward-looking (applies starting the quarter after the calculation period). We will update the exhibit to state "prospective adjustment" explicitly. That prevents retroactive refunds; credits only apply to future invoices unless both parties agree otherwise.

- Earnback formula: we can clarify the formula. Proposed: earnback = min( capped_amount, (committed_monthly_fee - billed_fee_for_period) * (months_under_floor / committed_months) ). We are ok capping cumulative earnback to 25% of the total fees billed in the 12-month lookback window. Putting Karthik on copy to confirm this cap makes sense financially.

- Trueup window: 6 months is reasonable from Redwood's perspective if NovaPlex agrees to an interim settlement threshold (e.g., if variance > 40%, settle within 30 days). Karthik — can you confirm we can operationalize a 6-month trueup with 30-day provisional settlement?

I've attached the pricing workbook with a worked example so everyone can see the math.

Next steps: Lauren / Karthik to propose redline text we can insert into Exhibit B, then we can push a DocuSign update.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
attachments: pricing-workbook-npx.xlsx (xlsx)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Contracts (NovaPlex) <contracts@novaplex.io>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovaPlex - Order Form redline: pricing exhibit questions

Marta / Connor — thanks. From a contract redact perspective I recommend the following practical edits to avoid open-ended liabilities while keeping the commercial intent intact. Below are redline-friendly snippets you can drop into Exhibit B.

1) Anchor band (prospective): replace the existing paragraph with: "Anchor Band Adjustment: The anchor band shall be calculated on a rolling three-month trailing basis and shall apply prospectively beginning the first day of the next billing quarter. Any adjustments shall not create an obligation for retroactive refunds unless expressly agreed in writing by both parties."

2) Earnback cap & calculation: proposed replacement language: "Earnback Credit: In the event Customer's billed usage for any billing month falls below the Floor, Customer shall be eligible for an earnback credit computed as follows: Earnback = max(0, (Floor - BilledUsage) / Floor) * MonthlyCommitment. Cumulative earnback credits shall not exceed 20% of TotalFees billed to Customer in the 12 months immediately preceding the credit. Any credits exceeding this cap must be mutually agreed and treated as a separate commercial concession."

Rationale: 20% cap is conservative and easier for finance to model than a 25% variable cap. It protects Redwood cashflow and aligns with typical enterprise practice.

3) Trueup: counterproposal: "Settlement & Trueup: The parties shall perform a reconciliation on a semi-annual basis (every six months). If variance between committed and actual billed usage exceeds 40% for the reconciliation period, the parties shall effect an interim settlement within 30 days of the reconciliation date. A final trueup shall occur within six months of the end of the applicable contract year."

I've attached a brief proposed redline (redline-proposal-npx.docx) with the insertions above. Neha — feel free to refine the legalese; once we have alignment on the commercial numbers from Karthik, we should be good to finalize.

—Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
attachments: redline-proposal-npx.docx (docx)

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Contracts (NovaPlex) <contracts@novaplex.io>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovaPlex - Order Form redline: pricing exhibit questions

Marta / team — following up with legal's position after reviewing Lauren's suggested language and Karthik's finance feedback (Karthik confirmed modeling supports a 20% cap). Key points / edits from legal: 

- Accept prospectivity for the Anchor Band as edited by Lauren. We will include an explicit "no retroactivity" sentence and a mutual exception carve-out for cases of fraud or manifest error.

- Accept the 20% cumulative earnback cap, but we will add a 24-month sunset on the right to accrue earnback credits (so credits cannot be accumulated beyond a 2-year window) to limit long-tail exposure. Suggested clause: "Accrual Period & Sunset: Earnback credits may be accrued for a maximum period of twenty-four (24) months from the Effective Date of the Order Form; thereafter, no new credits shall accrue absent mutual written agreement."

- Trueup language: legal accepts semi-annual reconciliation with interim 30-day settlement if variance > 40%. We will add an administrative fee clause for disputes (e.g., "disputed reconciliations shall not delay settlement of undisputed amounts").

Please confirm that NovaPlex is OK with (a) 20% cap, (b) 24-month earnback sunset, and (c) interim settlement process. Once NovaPlex confirms, Connor / Lauren — please push the agreed redline into DocuSign and reference HubSpot deal NPX-2026-07-43.

Proposed sample insert for Exhibit B (to reduce back-and-forth):
"Earnback Accrual & Cap: Customer's cumulative earnback credits under this Order Form shall not exceed twenty percent (20%) of TotalFees billed during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding any credit. Earnback credits may accrue for a maximum period of twenty-four (24) months from the Effective Date; credits accruing after such period shall be null and void unless otherwise agreed in writing. Any interim settlement resulting from a reconciliation shall be due within thirty (30) days and shall not be stayed by any ongoing dispute except to the extent the parties have agreed otherwise in writing."

Happy to take final redline in DocuSign.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachments: none
